channel.title: Cutefish
channel.description: Cutefish, also known as CutefishOS, is a Linux distribution built around Cutefish Desktop, a calm, fast desktop environment with its own compositor, toolkit and applications.

item.title: Mac apps on Cutefish: the first milestone
item.description: Reef has reached its first milestone. Real Mac apps install from their disk images and run completely, from a text editor and a terminal to a feed reader with a real web engine.

item.title: The Mac version of Ghostty, on Linux
item.description: Ghostty comes in a Mac version and a Linux version. On Cutefish you can run either. We put them side by side and explain why we reach for the Mac one.

item.title: Running Mac apps on Cutefish
item.description: Cutefish will be able to run apps made for the Mac, menu bar apps included. What that takes, how it differs from Darling and Wine, and what runs so far.

item.title: Letting agents use the desktop
item.description: How to let Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex or another agent see the Cutefish desktop and use its pointer and keyboard, with your permission.

item.title: How Cutefish packages are built, and how to check them
item.description: Cutefish packages and ISOs are built in the open by a public workflow, signed only by that workflow, and every file can be traced back to the build that made it.
